record.title: Rwanda restriction at Gatuna and on travel to Uganda
record.scope: Gatuna/Katuna crossing; broader restrictions on Rwandan travel to Uganda
record.crossings: Gatuna/Katuna; selective-permission reporting also names Kagitumba/Mirama Hills, where its detailed interview is situated. Cyanika evidence is contextual, not a claim that every phase applied at every gate.
record.direction: Rwandan exit to Uganda especially restricted; practical effects on both directions.
record.movement: Traders, cargo and passengers; resumption initially prioritised cargo and returnees.
record.exceptions: Foreigners crossed during 2019 Rwandan departure denials. January 2020 reporting describes selective accepted-reason permission. January 2022 inward cargo, citizens and returning residents were exceptions. Later bus and local-ID travel had different conditions.
record.enforcement: Reuters, AFP and Anadolu report limited observed crossings on 31 January.
record.official_rationale: Initial RRA heavy-truck diversion officially cited construction; later reclosure reporting cites structural cracks through an unnamed officer. Rwanda also alleged harassment of nationals and Ugandan support for dissidents, which Uganda disputed. These explanations belong to different accounts and should not be collapsed. Contemporary officials called the passenger warning advisory and attributed it to alleged insecurity; enforcement is separately documented. COVID explains stated 2022 exceptions and testing; national policy is GL04.
record.context: Diplomatic dispute; reopening followed bilateral contacts and Muhoozi Kainerugaba visit.
record.uncertainty: Passenger denial is documented by March 1, 2019; exact first onset remains unresolved. Dated denials and selective permissions do not establish a continuous 2019–2022 all-traffic closure. Preserve February 28 freight diversion, June 10–22 truck trial, January 31, 2022 cargo/returnee permission, March 7 outgoing bus and later local-shopping relaxation as different scopes. Freight eligibility remains contested; national COVID policy is GL04.
